title: Plural of one-syllable diphthong words
summary: For these one-syllable diphthong words, drop the first vowel and add -ita/-itä: työ (“work”) → töitä.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

A diphthong is two different vowels pronounced in one syllable. In these words ending in ie, uo or yö, drop the first vowel of the diphthong and add -ita/-itä to the remaining vowel. This rule concerns the selected one-syllable family, not longer words ending in two vowels.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

examples.english: work · drop y from yö; add -itä
steps: Drop y from yö and add -itä: työ → töitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “work”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: road · drop i from ie; add -itä
steps: Drop i from ie and add -itä: tie → teitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “road”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: night · drop y from yö; add -itä
steps: Drop y from yö and add -itä: yö → öitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “night”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: belt · drop y from yö; add -itä
steps: Drop y from yö and add -itä: vyö → vöitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “belt”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: swamp · drop u from uo; add -ita
steps: Drop u from uo and add -ita: suo → soita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “swamp”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Drop the first vowel, not the second.
Do not copy the unchanged-base singular -ta/-tä form.
Keep ö and ä in töitä, öitä and vöitä.
